newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas rises in Q3 on good demand from one buyer.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas rises in Q3 on good demand from one buyer.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market saw stronger prices in the third quarter as one large player emerged to buy big volumes, traders and brokers said.

"It ran up very quickly in the space of about an hour this morning," said a trader. A single buyer bought at least three lots of Q3 gas at 10.40 pence a therm in volumes ranging from 25,000 th/d to 200,000 th/d. And there were also rumours on the market that deals had been done at 10.25 pence and 10.375 pence.

There was a lot of volume offered at 10.50 pence for the third quarter, with one trader saying that around 600,000 th/d was available at this level. But it was not thought this price was reached, with the buyer managing to fill requirements at 10.40 pence. By the close, offers were reported down to 10.40 pence, with bids coming from 10.35 pence.

Other periods were relatively quiet. The first quarter next year was discussed in a slightly wider range than on Tuesday, with bids down to 15.80 pence and offers nudging up slightly to 16.00 pence. But no deals were reported from the quarter.

The short term market was quiet, with only occasional trades seen for the day ahead, the balance of the month and other early periods. Only a single May trade was confirmed, at 10.25 pence a therm. By contrast, there was keen interest for May gas on the IPE futures market.

A total of 160 lots were done in May on the IPE at between 10.20 and 10.30 pence, out of a total of only 215 lots done for any period. Futures brokers said that most of the trade was done by two companies.

Mild weather is further reducing the volumes of gas consumed. Transco forecasts that on Thursday, demand is set at 199 mcm, only 46 percent of peak day demand. And the temperature is forecast at 11.0 Celsius, up from a seasonal normal 9.0 Celsius.
